title: Differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into midbrain dopaminergic neurons
author: Nishimura, Ásgrímsdóttir, et al.
materials: Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody

steps.title: Coat plate and thaw cells
steps.instruction: Prepare a LN521 coating, thaw the hESC cryovial, centrifuge, resuspend, seed the cells, and change medium the next day.

substeps.instruction: Mix 100 µL LN521 with 1,400 µL PBS(+Ca²⁺/​+Mg²⁺) (final coating 1 µg/cm²) and add to one well of a 6‑well plate; incubate at 37 °C for ≥2 h (optional: coat at 4 °C overnight, 15–22 h).

Place a cryovial containing ≈500,000 hESCs in a 37 °C water bath and thaw until half‑thawed, then transfer the cells to a 15‑mL tube containing 10 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium (do NOT fully thaw to avoid cell death).
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 180 g for 3–5 min at room temperature (20–25 °C).
While the cells spin, wash the coated well twice with PBS(+Ca²⁺/​+Mg²⁺) and add 2 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium supplemented with 10 µM Y‑27632 (ROCK inhibitor).
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium + 10 µM Y‑27632.
Seed the cells into the coated well in a final volume of 3 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium + 10 µM Y‑27632.
Incubate overnight; the next day replace the medium with 3 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium without Y‑27632.

steps.title: Maintain hESC culture
steps.instruction: Keep the cells in NutriStem hPSC XF medium, changing medium daily and adjusting volume as the culture expands.

substeps.instruction: Change the culture medium daily.
Increase the medium volume from 3 mL up to 8 mL as the cells grow to prevent the medium from turning yellow.
Maintain cells at 70–80 % confluency before the next passage.

steps.title: Passage hESCs
steps.instruction: Detach, count, reseed, and optionally cryopreserve hESCs following a detailed series of actions.

substeps.instruction: Mix 100 µL LN521 with 1,400 µL PBS(+Ca²⁺/​+Mg²⁺) and coat a new well of a 6‑well plate at 37 °C for ≥2 h.
Discard the spent medium from the culture and wash the cells twice with PBS(‑Ca²⁺/‑Mg²⁺).
Add 1 mL TrypLE Select to the well and incubate at 37 °C for 4 min.
Gently pipette to obtain a single‑cell suspension, add 1 mL defined trypsin inhibitor (DTI) to inactivate TrypLE, and collect the cells in a 15‑mL tube.
Centrifuge at 180 g for 3–5 min at room temperature (20–25 °C).
While the cells spin, wash the coated well twice with PBS(‑Ca²⁺/‑Mg²⁺) and add 1 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium + 10 µM Y‑27632.
After centrifugation, discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium + 10 µM Y‑27632.
Count cells using a hemocytometer.
Seed 50,000 cells per well in 2 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium + 10 µM Y‑27632.
The following day replace the medium with 2 mL NutriStem hPSC XF medium without Y‑27632.
Change the medium daily until cells reach 70–80 % confluency (typically 6–7 days).
Repeat the entire passage procedure at least once more (usually yielding 2–3 × 10⁶ cells per 6‑well when 70–80 % confluent).
Optional: Freeze excess cells. Resuspend the dissociated cells at 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL in STEM‑CELLBANKER GMP‑Grade.
Aliquot 0.5 mL (≈500,000 cells) into each cryovial, place the vials in a −80 °C Cryo1°C freezing container, and store overnight.
Transfer the vials to liquid‑nitrogen storage the next day for long‑term preservation.

description: Prepare all stocks and media listed in the materials and equipment section before starting cell culture. If you use reagents from alternative suppliers, you must validate them before starting the experiments. All steps should be performed under sterile conditions in a Class II biosafety cabinet. Cells should be cultivated in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.Note: Work with hESCs should be performed in compliance with local and national ethical rules, regulatory requirements, and international guidelines.
